messages:
Anya: Quick UX thread — compact form on dashboard: inline errors vs top summary for short forms (2–3 fields). Thoughts on required marker + a11y announce? Mike: I lean inline for quick fixability. On mobile inline errors can push layout and hide CTA though. Jess: Inline under the field works. But let's avoid big multi-line error copy inline — keep it one line + link to details. Priya: Accessibility: do not rely on visual-only markers. Use aria-required=true and ensure errors are announced (role="alert" or aria-live="assertive"). Tom: Implementation note: we can toggle `aria-invalid` and render `
Please enter a valid email
` — that gets read automatically. Anya: About required markers: asterisk alone feels terse. Proposal: asterisk + 'required' in the form legend/help so screen readers get context. Mike: For destructive actions (bulk delete) copy options: 'Type DELETE to confirm' vs checkbox. Typed reduces accidents but adds friction. Jess: From a dev POV typed confirm is straightforward. Add server-side validation too. Example client check: `if (confirmInput.trim().toUpperCase() === 'DELETE') submit()` Priya: Ensure typed input has proper label and is announced on error; avoid using placeholder as a label — that breaks SR focus. Anya: Proposal: Inline errors for compact forms (<=3 fields); top summary for long flows. Required marker: asterisk + explicit legend + aria-required. Destructive: threshold-based typed-confirm (e.g., >20 items requires typing). Tom: I'll prototype a compact mobile variant: truncate error text with a 'More' link that opens full error in a modal (still announced). Mike: Sounds good. Tagging @product for sign-off :thumbsup: Product: Quick thumbs — agree with threshold typed-confirm. Minor copy tweak: use 'permanently delete' for clarity.
